subject: Business Models
title: Usage-Based Limits
description: A quick, practical guide to Usage-Based Limits.

hook.text: GitHub is free for unlimited public repos. Private repos? Free too. So where's the paywall? Teamwork.

buildup.text: Usage-based limits restrict volume: API calls, storage, team members, or compute hours.

discovery.text: The genius is that usage grows with business success. As you scale, you naturally cross the free threshold.

twist.text: AWS's free tier costs Amazon money—but users who start free on AWS rarely leave as they scale.

climax.text: Usage-based freemium aligns conversion with customer success. You only pay when you're getting real value.

punchline.text: Free until you grow. Usage-based paywalls reward success with invoices.

quiz.question: Why is usage-based freemium effective?
options: Conversion aligns with the customer's growing needs

details.summary: Usage-based limits restrict free tier access by consumption metrics like storage, API calls, messages, or compute hours rather than features. Dropbox limits free storage to 2GB, GitHub limits free CI minutes, and OpenAI limits free GPT queries. Users upgrade when they hit their usage ceiling.
details.whyItMatters: Usage-based limits create natural conversion triggers that align with growing customer value. As users get more value from the product.
takeaways: Free access is restricted by consumption thresholds rather than features
Users upgrade naturally as their usage grows beyond free tier limits
Usage limits align upgrade timing with customer value realization

faq.question: Why are usage-based limits more effective than feature gates for some products?
faq.answer: They give all users access to the full product experience, ensuring everyone understands its value. Conversion happens naturally as usage grows rather than through frustrating feature restrictions. Power users who get the most value convert first, which is the optimal targeting outcome.

faq.question: How do companies set the right usage limits for free tiers?
faq.answer: Analyze usage distributions to find the threshold where casual users are satisfied and power users need more. Set limits that let most users stay free while converting the top 5-10% of users by consumption. The limit should be generous enough to demonstrate value but tight enough to drive upgrades.
